newsitem.title: USA: GTE sees a third of EPS growth from overseas.
newsitem.headline: GTE sees a third of EPS growth from overseas.

text.p: GTE Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Lee said Wednesday that he expected a third of GTE's earnings growth would come from international operations.
"We expect international to be a source of one third of earnings growth in the years ahead," Lee told a Reuters reporter in New York.
The company had no official statement Wednesday afternoon on how the death of its senior vice president of international operations Bruce Haddad would immediately affect its plans.
Haddad and his wife were among five people who died earlier Wednesday when their corporate jet crashed south of Guatemala City, aviation officials said.

GTE has put a great deal of emphasis on its international expansion, which started 20 years ago. GTE has interests in Venezuela, Argentina and the Dominican Republic and is the largest foreign investor in the Canadian telecomunications industry.

"I called Peru (where the Haddads were picked up) to confirm the list of passengers, who were Bruce Haddad and Mrs Dorothy Haddad," Ronald Peter Zineri, Guatemala's director of civil aviation, told Reuters, adding that three Venezuelan crew members also were killed.
The corporate jet, a Westwind 24 chartered from the Venezuelan company Inversiones Liftoff, slammed into the side of a mountain about 0330 local (0930 GMT), Zineri said.
"It was good weather, nine kilometers visibility, the tower told the pilot, and it's on tape, a few seconds before the accident that he was off course," Zineri said.
The crew was identified as pilot Carlos Izquierdo, Francisco Nieto and Rafael Ramon.
The plane had taken off from Caracas, Venezuela, picked up the Haddads in Lima, Peru, and was to make a stop in Guatemala City on its way to Dallas, Texas, officials said.
